statements.t: “Williams delivered another strong quarter as our teams continued to execute across a growing portfolio of critical energy infrastructure projects.

Year-to-date Adjusted EBITDA increased 9% year over year to $6.2 billion, reflecting the strength of our natural gas transmission, storage and gathering businesses and keeping us on track toward the upper half of our 2026 guidance range.

Our performance to date, combined with a growing slate of projects set to come online, gives us strong confidence in our ability to achieve our long-term 11% plus Adjusted EBITDA compound annual growth rate through 2030.”

As the first of many power projects, Socrates demonstrates our ability to deliver fast, reliable and scalable solutions for customers facing rapidly growing power demand, and we are actively working to commercialize additional power projects, which we expect to announce soon.
Across our broader portfolio, we announced new Transco projects and expansions, advanced a storage expansion at Clay Basin, and placed four pipeline projects into service.”
The company continues to expect 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $8.3 billion to $8.5 billion and growth capex between $7.3 billion and $7.9 billion.
